_about: Avatar body size and positioning. Every value says where it came from. Segment lengths are fractions of standing height.
height_note: Mid-range adult. Change this to test a shorter or taller avatar.

segment_ratios._source: Drillis & Contini (1966) segment-length ratios, as tabulated in Winter, Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement

standing._note: null = use the ratio / the trunk card. Hip height = hip_height ratio x height.

seated_wheelchair._note: Hip pivot = typical manual wheelchair seat height 0.48 m (19 in) + ~0.09 m to the hip joint. Forward trunk lean capped at 30 degrees for seated balance.

approach._about: Distance from the avatar's hip centre (on the floor) to the wall, in metres.
approach._note: Standing forward: toes at the wall. Wheelchair forward: footrests at the wall. Wheelchair side: side of the chair ~0.1 m from the wall, which is inside the ADA 308.3 side-reach 10 in (255 mm) limit.

limb_clearance_m._about: How far the centre line of the arm (shoulder to wrist) must stay from a wall or counter. The arm has thickness; only the hand may touch the surface.
limb_clearance_m._note: About half the thickness of an adult forearm. Estimate: replace with a sourced forearm/upper-arm breadth.

doorway_clear_width_m._about: Clear width a door needs for each mobility aid. null = not sourced yet, so doorway results for that aid are UNVERIFIED.

wheelchair.source: ADA 2010 Standards 404.2.3: 32 in (815 mm) minimum clear width

none.source: Shoulder width (0.259 x height) + 0.05 m each side

KAFO.source: Same as 'none'; the circumduction card adds the leg swing once it is sourced

crutches.source: U.S. Access Board, ADAAG (2002) Appendix A4.2.1(2): people who use walking aids can maneuver through clear width openings of 32 in (815 mm); they need 36 in (915 mm) for passageways
crutches.caution_source: First In Architecture, Metric Data 04: width of a person with crutches 840 mm (UK averages, no study named; estimate)

cane.source: U.S. Access Board, ADAAG (2002) Appendix A4.2.1(2): people who use walking aids can maneuver through clear width openings of 32 in (815 mm)

walker.source: U.S. Access Board, ADAAG (2002) Appendix A4.2.1(2): people who use walking aids can maneuver through clear width openings of 32 in (815 mm)
